title: Join policy orchestrator: temporal approvals, domain attestation rotation & selective SSO enforcement
creator: Laila Torres
description:
Problem: Current org/team onboarding controls are fragmented across invite workflows, domain verification, and SSO enforcement. Operators need fine-grained, time-bound controls for membership approvals, automatic domain attestation rotation, and a way to selectively require SSO for subsets of domains or team scopes.

Goal: Build a Join Policy Orchestrator service and admin UX that centralizes invite policy rules, supports temporal approval windows (e.g., 'auto-approve for 24h then require escalation'), domain attestation token rotation, domain reputation scoring for allowlist/denylist decisions, and per-domain SSO enforcement toggles. Ensure rich audit logging for every decision and rollbackable policy changes.

Scope: engineering implementation of the orchestrator API, datastore schemas, audit-log enrichment, admin-facing feature flags for selective SSO enforcement, and a phased rollout via feature-flagged canary routes. This ticket covers the core orchestration primitives and the backend integration; separate tickets will cover full console UX polish and long-term analytics.
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine accepts multiple rule types: temporal_approval, domain_allowlist, domain_denylist, sso_enforce, guest_expiry
Admin API endpoints to create/modify policies with strong validation and 'dry-run' mode
Join requests are routed through the orchestrator and annotated in audit logs with policy_id, decision, matched_rule, and evaluation_latency
Domain attestation tokens rotate automatically every 30 days and can be manually rotated via admin API; rotations are logged
Selective SSO enforcement: teams/orgs can opt to require SSO for invites from specified domains without affecting other domains
Rate limiting of invites per-sender and per-domain with backoff and observable metrics
End-to-end integration test demonstrating auto-approve -> escalation after window expiration
Security review completed and remediation items tracked before GA rollout
tasks: Design: policy schema and evaluation ordering (priority, conditions, temporal window)
Implement: orchestrator service with policy evaluation cache and fast-path for common rules
Integrate: wire into invite delivery flow and org-join API (pre-check + post-decision hooks)
Audit: extend audit logging schema with policy_id, matched_rules, token_version, and evaluator_trace
Auth: add RBAC v2 checks for who can create/modify policies (org-admin vs super-admin)
SSO: implement per-domain SSO toggle and enforcement middleware
Domain: implement attestation token lifecycle and reputation score ingestion job
Testing: unit tests, property tests for policy precedence, and integration test harness
Rollout: feature-flag controlled canary with telemetry and automatic rollback on increase in failed joins or latency

notes:
Design trade-offs: evaluating pre-evaluation caching vs. faster in-memory rule engine to avoid per-request DB hits. Chosen approach: lightweight LRU policy cache with cache-invalidation events on policy change to ensure eventual consistency.

Metrics to track: policy_eval_latency_ms, join_decisions_total{decision}, invite_rate_per_domain, attestation_rotation_success_rate.

Privacy: audit log entries will redact invitee email addresses for personal-data minimization unless the requester is an authorized auditor via RBAC v2.

Rollout plan: start with 5% orgs for dry-run policies (no enforcement), then 20% with SSO-only enforcement, then full enforcement after 2-week stability window.
